key_insight: The HOPE trial will test whether a shorter, dose-painted VMAT chemoradiation regimen can reduce acute gastrointestinal toxicity in stage I–IIB cervical cancer without compromising cancer control.
clinical_relevance: If successful, this approach could simplify treatment delivery and improve patient tolerance for women receiving definitive chemoradiation for cervical cancer.
method: Phase II, multi-center, open-label, randomized, parallel-group superiority trial in India
300 patients randomized 1:1 to hypofractionated dose-painted VMAT vs conventional VMAT
Both arms receive weekly cisplatin and image-guided brachytherapy; primary outcome is grade ≥2 GI toxicity
evidence_signal: The abstract describes a prospective randomized trial design with clearly defined toxicity and longer-term efficacy endpoints, but no outcome data are yet available because enrollment has not started.
watch_item: Because the study is open-label and compares different fractionation and chemotherapy schedules, implementation will depend on careful toxicity assessment and consistent brachytherapy/VMAT quality across centers.
paper_title: A phase II multi-center, open-label, randomized, parallel-group, superiority study to compare the acute toxicity of Hypofractionated dOse Painted External radiotherapy versus conventional external radiotherapy in patients with carcinoma cervix stage I - IIB. (HOPE)
